forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Greek and regional yields face structural aridification. Reaching $7,000 by March is highly likely as real inventory shortages bite.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Persistent Mediterranean heating and depletion of aquifers keep olive production highly volatile, easily keeping prices above historic normal ranges.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Severe European temperature anomalies continue to degrade groves. Water scarcity and structural deficits make reaching $7,000/mt a very realistic threshold by spring.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Persistent Southern European drought and climate stress keep olive harvests vulnerable, making a rebound above $7,000 highly plausible.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Severe European heat anomalies and regional Levantine supply disruptions support elevated Mediterranean olive oil prices toward $7,000/mt.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Persistent Mediterranean water tensions and Middle East harvest conflicts provide price support, though $7,000 remains a high barrier.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: The market indicates 38%. Olive oil prices plateaued and eased marginally last month, so I stay right beside the consensus.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Persistently high Mediterranean temperatures sustain supply vulnerability, but rebounding output in North Africa caps excessive price rallies.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Output recovery across Mediterranean producers gradually normalizes balance sheets, containing prices below $7,000/mt.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Reflationary ag trends provide underlying support, but olive oil lacks the broad spec momentum needed to comfortably push past $7,000.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Production recovery across key Mediterranean basins exerts steady downward pressure on grower prices, capping Greek olive oil below $7,000/mt.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Elevated prices have already prompted demand destruction and supply normalization. Rallies past $7,000 face severe fundamental headwinds.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rebuilding regional stocks and harvest arrivals through early 2027 should relieve price pressure, making levels above $7,000/mt difficult to sustain.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Greek mills will be flush with freshly pressed oil through February. Seasonal volume additions cap upside well short of $7,000 by early spring.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Growers adapt to heat, and recovering harvest volumes in Southern Europe will prevent prices from sustaining above $7,000.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Breaking $7,000 demands renewed supply shocks. Markets have already absorbed regional harvest friction; prices should hold or drift toward the historical mean.
